Respiratory Illness Outbreak Hits UAE Metals & Mining Sector, Operations Disrupted

A respiratory illness outbreak has struck several sites in the United Arab Emirates' Metals & Mining industry, forcing temporary shutdowns and causing production slowdowns as companies work to contain the spread among workers, industry sources said Tuesday.

The outbreak, first detected late last week at a copper smelting facility in the Al Dhafra region, has now affected at least four major mining and processing operations across Abu Dhabi and Ras Al Khaimah, according to the UAE Metals & Mining Association. The disease, presenting with flu-like symptoms and shortness of breath, has so far led to the hospitalization of more than 50 employees, with hundreds more under observation or in quarantine.

"Protecting our workforce is the top priority," said Ahmed al-Ketbi, spokesperson for Emirates Strategic Mining. "We have suspended operations at two sites and implemented strict health protocols, including on-site medical screening and isolation areas for those showing symptoms."

Production at several bauxite and copper processing plants has slowed significantly, with staffing levels reduced by up to 40% at some facilities. According to industry sources, output from the sector’s largest alumina refinery has dropped by an estimated 25% since the outbreak began.

Union representatives reported growing concern among workers. "There is anxiety on the ground," said Noura Al Suwaidi, regional organizer for the Metals & Mining Workers Union. "People are worried about their health, and many have families back in their home countries."

The UAE Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology is coordinating with local health authorities and company medical teams to monitor the situation. "We are actively supporting all affected companies and ensuring that containment measures are robust," a ministry official said.

Industry analysts warned that a prolonged outbreak could have significant implications for the sector’s export commitments and operational planning. "If these disruptions continue, we could see delays in project timelines and a tightening of supply from UAE producers," said Malik Hassan, an independent mining consultant based in Dubai.

As of Tuesday evening, most affected sites remained partially operational with enhanced safety protocols in place. Industry leaders said they are reviewing contingency plans daily, as health experts continue to investigate the source and transmission of the illness.
